studyField: East and Southeastern European Studies (Balkan Studies)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was the most chaotic and disorganized exchange I have ever experienced, the help I needed during the exchange was mainly from my professors in Copenhagen and the professors ind Zagreb. The international office in Copenhagen and Zagreb did not point me in any direction regarding the help i needed, therefore i contacted my professors in both Copenhagen and Zagreb who, once again, were the only ones who actually helped me solving the problems I had in Zagreb. I know for sure that I am not the only one who has been having these kinds of issues during the exchange, not only this year, but also the previous years and the students who are just now applying for the following exchange are also in need for more guidance. It seems to me as that the administration/international office, in this case Copenhagen and Zagreb, do not communicate very well which leeds to sending students abroad who has to solve problems that should have not even had to become problems in the first place, these kind of issues should have been avoided before the arrival at the study destination. I sincerely hope that this will not be happening for other students in the future.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I signed up for subjects from Denmark, but when I arrived in Zagreb I was told that only 1 of the 6 subjects I had applied for were available. This was because the others were electives and there were not enough enrollees. This is understandable, of course, but it was something I was told first when I already arrived at the University of Zagreb. Neither the University of Copenhagen nor the University of Zagreb made me aware that the subjects were only optional. In addition, there was no help to be found in relation to finding new subjects, I was told the following on Croaticum: '' You can go to our website and find other subjects or knock on doors and ask teachers if you can follow their subjects. '' The links i got from them did not work. The only help I got with this was from a professor back in Copehagen, neither the international department in Copenhagen nor Zagreb helped me with this.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The first thing that needs to happen at all is more communication between the universities, and far more information for the students who are going on an exchange. All this has not been properly addressed at all. If this exchange is to be obligatory, as it is for some of us, then things must work as well.
